resources.string: This key lives only on this phone. If it is lost or deleted, the identity is lost: receipts already issued stay valid if you exported the public key, but new evidence will carry a different identity. There is no cloud copy, on purpose.
Your identity is an ML-DSA-87 signing key created now, on this phone, and it signs every evidence item. There is no server and no sign-up: the key is the identity, nothing else.

What the app claims about itself, checked on this phone.

Internet: yes, only to send fingerprints (32 bytes) to the OpenTimestamps calendars and receive proofs (directly or, if you turn it on, only over Tor). Never photos, videos or files. Microphone: only while you record a video or audio; if you deny it, video is recorded without sound and audio cannot be recorded.
Calls, video calls and private messages live in X39 Communications, a separate app. This keeps this app small and verifiable, and each app has its own permissions.
X39 Communications is not installed. It is in closed beta until November.

Fingerprints go out only through Tor (Orbot). It hides your IP address from the calendars. Your carrier can see that you use Tor; in some countries that draws attention. If Orbot is not running, fingerprints wait.
